what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Cuba in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 122494 Cuban asylum seekers in the United States, 42.5% of all asylum seekers from Cuba.
Refugees from Cuba, a separate group, live mostly in Mexico and the United States.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for Cuba, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2022 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 3049 asylum seekers.
The figure reached its highest point, 230055, at the end of 2023 and was lower by the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
